blocks.text: 1. Chain Of Thought
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785447581445-703391810.png

Few-Shot Prompting's closing recap pointed forward to this topic. Chain of Thought, covering how prompting can encourage step by step reasoning, moves beyond demonstrating format to demonstrating a process.
It instructs the model to reason through intermediate steps before giving a final answer, a technique built on reasoning rather than formatting.
2. Why Jumping Straight To An Answer Fails

blocks.alt: Why Jumping Straight To An Answer Fails
blocks.text: https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785447581445-450477499.png

As with the gap between few-shot and zero-shot prompting covered in Few-Shot Prompting, questions that require comparing or combining multiple retrieved facts can trip up a model asked for an immediate answer.
Skipping intermediate reasoning raises the chance of wrongly combining correct facts.

blocks.content: {"headers":["Approach","Risk on multi-fact questions"],"rows":[["Immediate answer","Higher chance of wrongly combining correct facts"],["Step by step reasoning","Each combination step is made explicit and checkable"]]}

blocks.text: 3. Asking The Model To Reason Step By Step

blocks.alt: Asking The Model To Reason Step By Step
blocks.text: https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785447581611-407027684.png
Adding an instruction like think step by step encourages the model to work through the retrieved context first.
The model produces intermediate reasoning text before arriving at the final answer.
4. Grounding Each Reasoning Step In Context

blocks.alt: Grounding Each Reasoning Step In Context
blocks.text: https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785447581611-921843879.png
As with instructing the model to use source labels, covered in System Prompting, each reasoning step should reference the specific retrieved fact it relies on.
This keeps the model reasoning from cited evidence rather than unstated, ungrounded assumptions.

blocks.title: Note
blocks.content: A reasoning step that states which retrieved fact it relies on is far easier to audit than one that draws on an unstated assumption instead.

blocks.text: 5. Multi-Hop Questions Benefit Most
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785447581611-931762865.png
As with multi-hop retrieval gathering facts across several documents, covered in Retrieval, a question needing several chained facts benefits most from explicit reasoning.
Each hop of the answer depends on the previous one being correct.
6. Reasoning Token Cost
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785447581612-844053968.png
As covered in Token Budgeting, every part of the prompt takes space, and the intermediate reasoning text itself consumes real output tokens.
That is a real latency and cost tradeoff against simpler direct answers.

blocks.title: Note
blocks.content: Generating several sentences of intermediate reasoning before the final answer adds real output tokens and real latency compared with a direct answer, a cost worth weighing against the accuracy gained.

blocks.text: 7. Exposed Reasoning Can Leak Errors
Showing the full reasoning trace to the end user risks exposing an incorrect intermediate step.
That risk holds even when the final answer itself still lands correctly.
8. Combining Chain Of Thought With Citations
As with the citation format consistency covered in Citation Prompting, each reasoning step can cite the specific source it draws from.
That makes both the reasoning and the final answer independently checkable.

blocks.content: {"headers":["Element","What it makes checkable"],"rows":[["Cited reasoning step","Whether that specific intermediate step is grounded correctly"],["Final answer","Whether the conclusion follows from the cited steps"]]}

blocks.text: 9. Recognizing When Chain Of Thought Prompting Is Worth The Added Tokens

blocks.alt: Recognizing When Chain Of Thought Prompting Is Worth The Added Tokens
blocks.text: https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785447581612-168290510.png
Multi-hop or comparison questions benefit most from explicit reasoning.
Simple, single-fact lookups rarely need visible reasoning at all.
10. Worked Example
The example below demonstrates a chain of thought prompt for a multi-hop comparison question.

code.content:
sources = {
    1: "The Falcon plan costs twenty dollars per month and includes ten projects.",
    2: "The Eagle plan costs thirty five dollars per month and includes unlimited projects.",
}

def build_chain_of_thought_prompt(sources, query):
    # build the labeled context block so each fact can be cited by number
    context_block = "\n".join(f"[{k}] {v}" for k, v in sources.items())
    return (
        f"Context:\n{context_block}\n\n"
        f"Question: {query}\n"
        "Think step by step. For each step, cite the source number it relies on. "
        "Then give a final answer on its own line starting with Answer:"
    )

query = "Which plan is cheaper and by how much?"
prompt = build_chain_of_thought_prompt(sources, query)
print("Chain of thought prompt:\n")
print(prompt)

simulated_reasoning = (
    "Step 1 [1]: The Falcon plan costs twenty dollars per month.\n"
    "Step 2 [2]: The Eagle plan costs thirty five dollars per month.\n"
    "Step 3: Thirty five minus twenty equals fifteen.\n"
    "Answer: The Falcon plan is cheaper by fifteen dollars per month [1][2]."
)
print("\nSimulated reasoning trace:\n")
print(simulated_reasoning)

blocks.title: Note
blocks.content: Running this example shows each reasoning step citing the specific source it depends on before the final answer combines them.

blocks.text: 11. Common Mistakes

items: Asking for step by step reasoning on simple single-fact questions that do not need it.
Letting reasoning steps draw on unstated assumptions instead of the retrieved context.
Exposing the full reasoning trace to end users without reviewing it for leaked errors.
Forgetting to cite sources within each reasoning step, losing the ability to check it.

blocks.text: 12. Key Takeaways

items: Chain of thought prompting instructs the model to reason through intermediate steps before answering.
Jumping straight to an answer raises the risk of wrongly combining correct facts.
An instruction like think step by step encourages visible intermediate reasoning.
Each reasoning step should reference the specific retrieved fact it relies on.
Multi-hop questions needing several chained facts benefit most from explicit reasoning.
Intermediate reasoning text consumes real output tokens, adding latency and cost.
Exposing the full reasoning trace risks surfacing an incorrect intermediate step.
Citing sources within each reasoning step keeps both reasoning and answer checkable.
